functions.name: ctranslate2::VocabularyMap::VocabularyMap
functions.description: Constructs a VocabularyMap by loading a vocabulary mapping model from a text stream. Each line in the stream should associate a source n-gram with a list of candidate target tokens, of the form: "<n-gram>\t candidate1 candidate2 ... candidateN". The constructor uses the provided Vocabulary to resolve candidate tokens (and possibly n-grams) to vocabulary IDs and prepares internal mapping rules for later candidate retrieval.
requirements: map_file must be a readable input stream positioned at the beginning of the mapping data and remain valid during construction.
map_file content must follow the documented format: one mapping per line, with a source n-gram, a tab character, and a space-separated list of candidate tokens.
The provided vocabulary must correspond to the tokenization used in map_file so that tokens referenced in the file can be resolved to IDs.
Behavior for tokens or candidates not present in the vocabulary is unspecified in the header; callers should ensure all tokens used in map_file exist in the vocabulary.
Must be called before any calls to get_candidates.

functions.name: ctranslate2::VocabularyMap::get_candidates
functions.signature: std::vector<size_t> ctranslate2::VocabularyMap::get_candidates(const std::vector<std::vector<std::string>>& source_tokens, const std::vector<std::vector<size_t>>& target_prefix_ids) const
functions.description: Returns an ordered list of candidate target token IDs for the given inputs. It maps input source tokens (batched, tokenized text) and corresponding target prefix token ID sequences to a set of possible next target tokens based on the mapping rules loaded at construction.
requirements: Must be called on a VocabularyMap instance that was successfully constructed from a valid mapping file.
The returned vector is ordered (as documented).
source_tokens is a batch: each inner vector represents a tokenized source sequence (strings).
target_prefix_ids is a batch: each inner vector represents a sequence of target token IDs (size_t) that form the current target prefix for the corresponding source example.
The batch sizes of source_tokens and target_prefix_ids should match (inferred from parallel batching in the signature).
Token strings in source_tokens and token IDs in target_prefix_ids should be consistent with the Vocabulary used at construction (i.e., tokenization and ID mapping align).
All token IDs involved are expected to be within the vocabulary range [0, vocabulary_size); the header does not specify behavior for out-of-range IDs.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ScoringResult::cumulated_score
functions.description: Returns the sum of all per-token scores stored in tokens_score. Intended to provide the total (unnormalized) score for the sequence represented by this ScoringResult. Usage: call on a populated ScoringResult to get the aggregate score.
requirements: No preconditions beyond ScoringResult being a valid object.
tokens_score may be empty; in that case the function returns 0.f by definition.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ScoringResult::normalized_score
functions.description: Returns the average per-token score, computed as cumulated_score() divided by the number of tokens (tokens_score.size()). If there are no tokens (size is 0), returns 0.f. Usage: call on a populated ScoringResult when a length-normalized score is needed.
requirements: No preconditions beyond ScoringResult being a valid object.
If tokens_score is empty, the function returns 0.f (no error is raised).

functions.name: ctranslate2::score_sequences
functions.signature: std::vector<ctranslate2::ScoringResult> ctranslate2::score_sequences(ctranslate2::layers::Decoder& decoder, ctranslate2::layers::DecoderState& state, const std::vector<std::vector<size_t>>& sequences, const ctranslate2::Vocabulary& vocabulary, const ctranslate2::dim_t preferred_size_multiple = 1, const ctranslate2::dim_t offset = 0)
functions.description: Scores a batch of token id sequences using the provided decoder and state. The sequences are internally split into decoder input and output parts, so each sequence must include all special tokens such as start and end tokens. Returns one ScoringResult per input sequence, containing token strings and per-token scores. Typical usage: initialize/prepare a Decoder and DecoderState for a model, provide sequences of token ids aligned with the provided Vocabulary, and call this function to obtain scores.
requirements: sequences must include all tokens required by the model, including start and end tokens, because the function internally splits them into decoder input and output.
decoder must be a valid ctranslate2::layers::Decoder instance; state must be a valid ctranslate2::layers::DecoderState associated for use with that decoder (details not documented here).
vocabulary must correspond to the token id space of sequences (inferred from parameter types and naming; exact mapping rules are not documented).
preferred_size_multiple and offset have no documented constraints in this header; if unsure, use their defaults (1 and 0 respectively).

functions.name: ctranslate2::str_to_batch_type
functions.description: Converts a string to its corresponding BatchType enum value. Use to parse user/config inputs such as "Examples" or "Tokens" into an enum for batching logic. Exact accepted string forms and case sensitivity are not documented here.
requirements: Input batch_type must represent a valid BatchType; exact accepted values/casing are unknown from this header.
Callers should handle errors for unrecognized strings; behavior on invalid input is unknown from this header (e.g., exception vs. default).

functions.name: ctranslate2::BatchReader::get_next
functions.signature: std::vector<ctranslate2::Example> ctranslate2::BatchReader::get_next(const size_t max_batch_size, const ctranslate2::BatchType batch_type = ctranslate2::BatchType::Examples, const bool consider_padding = false);
functions.description: Fetches the next batch of examples from the reader according to the requested batching policy. Intended as the main batching API that groups examples by either example count or token count and may consider padding when building batches.
requirements: This method depends on successive calls to get_next_example() provided by the concrete subclass.
max_batch_size should be a meaningful positive size for batching; exact constraints are not specified in this header.
batch_type controls batching by examples or tokens; accepted values are BatchType::Examples or BatchType::Tokens.
If consider_padding is true, batching may account for padding length; exact behavior is not specified in this header.
Callers should be prepared to receive an empty vector when no more data is available.

functions.name: ctranslate2::BatchReader::get_next_example
functions.description: Consumes and returns the next Example from the data source. This is the primitive that concrete readers must implement; higher-level batching (get_next) is built on top of it.

Should return an empty Example when input is exhausted; exact end-of-stream signaling is not specified here.

functions.name: ctranslate2::BatchReader::num_examples
functions.description: Returns the total number of available examples, or 0 if not known. Default implementation returns 0.

functions.name: ctranslate2::TextLineReader::get_next_example
functions.description: Reads the next line from the bound std::istream and tokenizes it using the provided Tokenizer to produce a single-stream Example. If no line is available, returns an empty Example.
requirements: Underlying std::istream must be readable; end-of-file or read errors will yield an empty Example.

Tokenizer reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the TextLineReader instance.

functions.name: ctranslate2::VectorReader::VectorReader
functions.description: Constructs a VectorReader from a vector of single-stream examples (each inner vector is a sequence of tokens).

Each inner vector<string> represents one stream of tokens for a single Example.

functions.name: ctranslate2::VectorReader::VectorReader

requirements: Ownership of the provided examples vector is moved into the reader (by value).

functions.name: ctranslate2::VectorReader::get_next_example
functions.description: Returns and consumes the next Example from the internal vector. Advances an internal index until all examples are exhausted, after which subsequent calls return an empty Example.

functions.name: ctranslate2::VectorReader::num_examples
functions.description: Returns the total number of examples held by this VectorReader.
requirements: No special requirements; returns the size of the internal examples vector.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ParallelBatchReader::add
functions.description: Adds a BatchReader source to this ParallelBatchReader. Multiple sources can be combined; batching will draw from them in a reader-defined manner.
requirements: The reader pointer is transferred (moved) into the ParallelBatchReader; the caller must not use the pointer after passing it.

All added readers should remain valid within the ParallelBatchReader after transfer (owned by it).

functions.name: ctranslate2::ParallelBatchReader::get_next_example
functions.description: Consumes and returns the next Example aggregated from the added readers. The selection strategy among readers is not specified here.
requirements: At least one reader should be added before calling; otherwise behavior is undefined from this header.
Callers should handle an empty Example to signal exhaustion across sources.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ParallelBatchReader::num_examples
functions.description: Returns the total number of examples across all added readers, if known. Exact aggregation behavior is not specified in this header.
requirements: Depends on the underlying readers’ num_examples implementations; when unknown, the returned value may be 0.

functions.name: ctranslate2::Batch::num_examples
functions.description: Returns the number of examples contained in this Batch.
requirements: No special requirements; reflects examples.size().

functions.name: ctranslate2::Batch::empty
functions.description: Reports whether this Batch contains no examples.
requirements: No special requirements; equivalent to examples.empty().

functions.name: ctranslate2::Batch::get_stream
functions.description: Extracts the specified stream from all examples in the batch and returns it as a vector of token sequences. For multi-stream examples (e.g., source/target), index selects which stream to collect across the batch.

Callers should ensure each Example has at least index+1 streams to avoid undefined behavior in the implementation.

functions.name: ctranslate2::load_examples
functions.description: Builds a list of Example objects from a nested vector-of-streams input representation. Intended to convert raw tokenized data into Example structures for batching.
requirements: Input must be structured as a vector of examples, where each example is a vector of streams, and each stream is a vector of tokens (strings).
Ownership of the provided container is moved (by value).

functions.name: ctranslate2::rebatch_input
functions.signature: std::vector<ctranslate2::Batch> ctranslate2::rebatch_input(const std::vector<ctranslate2::Example>& examples, size_t max_batch_size = 0, ctranslate2::BatchType batch_type = ctranslate2::BatchType::Examples);
functions.description: Re-batches the given examples into new Batch objects with the specified maximum batch size. This function may also reorder examples to improve efficiency.
requirements: examples is a read-only input collection; it must remain valid during the call.
max_batch_size defines the batching capacity; exact constraints and behavior when 0 are not specified here.
batch_type selects batching by examples or tokens; only BatchType::Examples and BatchType::Tokens are defined.
Callers should not rely on the original order of examples, as the function may reorder them.

functions.name: ctranslate2::BufferedTranslationWrapper::BufferedTranslationWrapper
functions.signature: ctranslate2::BufferedTranslationWrapper::BufferedTranslationWrapper(std::shared_ptr<ctranslate2::Translator> translator, size_t max_batch_size, size_t buffer_timeout_in_micros, ctranslate2::TranslationOptions options = ctranslate2::TranslationOptions(), size_t max_buffer_size = 0)
functions.description: Constructs a wrapper around a Translator that buffers incoming translation requests and flushes them either when the buffer timeout elapses or when the buffer reaches the configured capacity. Intended to improve throughput by batching requests up to max_batch_size and, when max_buffer_size > max_batch_size, by sorting by length and re-batching. Use to submit asynchronous single or batched translation requests via translate_async or translate_batch_async.
requirements: translator must refer to a valid Translator instance (non-null shared_ptr).
max_batch_size controls the maximum batch size used when translating; inferred to be a positive, non-zero value.
buffer_timeout_in_micros specifies the buffer flush timeout in microseconds; zero or very small values may reduce buffering effectiveness (exact constraints unknown).
If max_buffer_size == 0, it defaults to max_batch_size (per class comment).
If max_buffer_size is set to a non-zero value, it should be greater than or equal to max_batch_size to allow re-batching (per class comment).

functions.name: ctranslate2::BufferedTranslationWrapper::~BufferedTranslationWrapper
functions.description: Destructor for the buffered wrapper. Cleans up internal resources, including the background buffering thread and any synchronization primitives. Typically ensures the buffering loop stops before object destruction.
requirements: Do not use the instance after destruction.

Behavior regarding outstanding futures at destruction time is not documented; callers should ensure any in-flight operations are completed or otherwise handle potential cancellation/exception (exact behavior unknown).

functions.name: ctranslate2::BufferedTranslationWrapper::translate_async
functions.description: Submits a single example for translation asynchronously. The call returns immediately with a future that becomes ready when the buffered batch containing this example is translated or when the buffer is flushed by timeout or capacity. The optional target argument can carry target-side tokens (e.g., prefix or constraints) if supported by the underlying Translator; exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: source is a sequence of tokens represented as strings; expected to be suitable input for the underlying Translator (exact tokenization and allowed content unknown).
target is optional; if provided, it should align with the Translator's expectations (semantics unknown).
The returned future must be waited on or otherwise handled by the caller to observe completion or errors.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are not specified; concurrent calls may be supported but are not guaranteed (unknown).

functions.name: ctranslate2::BufferedTranslationWrapper::translate_batch_async
functions.description: Submits a batch of examples for translation asynchronously. Returns one future per example. The wrapper buffers incoming batches and may sort/re-batch them internally before translation, flushing on timeout or when the buffer reaches capacity.
requirements: source is a batch of token sequences; each inner vector represents one example (exact tokenization and allowed content unknown).
If target is provided, its size should equal source.size(), and each inner target sequence should correspond to the example at the same index (semantics of target sequences are not documented).
The returned futures must be waited on or otherwise handled by the caller to observe completion or errors.
Batch size constraints at submission time are not documented; the wrapper will internally re-batch according to max_batch_size and max_buffer_size (details beyond the class comment unknown).

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::post
functions.signature:
template <typename Result, typename Func>
std::future<Result> ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::post(Func func)
functions.description: Posts a single callable to be executed on the first available model replica and returns a future for its single result. The callable must be invocable as Result(Replica&) and will be executed in a worker thread bound to a specific replica. Exceptions thrown by the callable are captured and will be rethrown when getting the future's value.
requirements: Func must be callable with signature Result(Replica&) and return a value convertible to Result.
The callable must be safe to run on a background thread (no reliance on thread-local state unless intended).
The replica used is selected by the pool; callers should not assume which replica executes the task.
If the callable throws, the exception will be stored in the future and rethrown on get().
Pool must be initialized with at least one replica (implied by construction); otherwise posting work is undefined/ill-formed.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::post_batch
functions.signature:
template <typename Result, typename Func>
std::vector<std::future<Result>> ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::post_batch(Func func, size_t num_results)
functions.description: Posts a batched callable to be executed on the first available replica and returns one future per expected result. The callable must be invocable as std::vector<Result>(Replica&) and should produce exactly num_results outputs for the submitted batch.
requirements: Func must be callable with signature std::vector<Result>(Replica&) and return a vector of results.
The returned std::vector<Result> from func must contain exactly num_results elements; otherwise the job will access out-of-range elements and cause undefined behavior.
num_results determines the number of futures allocated; choose it to match the callable's output size.
The callable must be safe to run on a background thread.
Exceptions thrown by the callable will be propagated to all corresponding futures.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::num_queued_batches
functions.description: Returns the number of batches currently queued in the pool's work queue (not yet being processed by workers). Useful for monitoring backpressure and queue depth.
requirements: Pool must be constructed; method is const and can be called at any time.
Value reflects the internal thread pool’s queued jobs.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::num_active_batches
functions.description: Returns the number of batches that are either queued or actively being processed by workers. This is a snapshot metric for current workload.
requirements: Pool must be constructed; method is const and can be called at any time.
Value is provided by the internal thread pool and may change concurrently.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::num_replicas
functions.description: Returns the number of parallel replicas managed by the pool (i.e., the number of worker threads).
requirements: Pool must be constructed; method is const and can be called at any time.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::detach_models
functions.description: Detaches and returns the models currently held by each replica worker, allowing callers to unload or replace models externally. After detaching, the workers no longer hold replicas.
requirements: Not thread-safe: callers must ensure no concurrent use of the pool (no in-flight jobs or other concurrent method calls).
Pool must contain at least one replica; returns a vector sized to num_replicas().
After detaching, previously posted jobs that access replicas would fail; ensure the queue is drained before calling.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::set_models
functions.description: Assigns a model to each replica worker, replacing any existing replicas. The models vector must match the number of replicas in the pool.
requirements: Not thread-safe: callers must ensure no concurrent use of the pool (no in-flight jobs or other concurrent method calls).
models.size() must equal num_replicas(); otherwise std::invalid_argument is thrown.
Each element of models must be non-null; it is dereferenced to construct a Replica and a null element will cause undefined behavior (dereference of null).

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::clear_cache
functions.description: Clears the memory allocator cache for each worker if an allocator is registered. Useful to release cached memory back to the system/device.
requirements: Not thread-safe: callers must ensure no concurrent use of the pool when calling this method.
Has no effect for workers without a registered allocator.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaPool<Replica>::get_first_replica
functions.description: Returns a reference to the first replica managed by the pool. Intended for introspection or accessing replica-level properties without posting a job.
requirements: Pool must own at least one initialized replica; otherwise downstream access in worker.replica() would throw.
The returned reference remains valid while the underlying worker holds the replica; do not call after detaching models or destroying the pool.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaWorker<Replica>::replica
functions.description: Returns a reference to the current replica object held by this worker. Throws std::runtime_error if no replica is available in the calling thread.
requirements: A replica must be set on this worker before calling; otherwise a std::runtime_error is thrown.
The caller must ensure the worker’s lifetime outlives usage of the returned reference.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaWorker<Replica>::set_model
functions.description: Constructs a new Replica from the provided model and stores it in the worker, replacing any existing replica.
requirements: model must be non-null; it is dereferenced to construct the Replica.
May replace an existing replica; callers should ensure no concurrent use of the previous replica when calling.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaWorker<Replica>::detach_model
functions.description: Detaches and returns the underlying model from the current replica, resetting the stored replica. If no replica is present, returns nullptr.
requirements: If a replica is present, it will be reset; subsequent calls to replica() will throw until a model is set again.
Callers should ensure no concurrent use of the replica when detaching.

functions.name: ctranslate2::ReplicaWorker<Replica>::allocator
functions.description: Returns the pointer to the memory Allocator registered for this worker thread, or nullptr if none. The allocator is set during worker initialization.
requirements: Allocator is initialized in the worker thread’s initialize(); before that it may be nullptr.
The returned pointer is owned by the system; callers must not delete it and must treat it as non-thread-safe unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: ctranslate2::primitives::compute_u8_compensation
functions.signature:
template <ctranslate2::Device D>
static void ctranslate2::primitives<D>::compute_u8_compensation(const int8_t* b,
                                        bool transpose_b,
                                        ctranslate2::dim_t k,
                                        ctranslate2::dim_t n,
                                        float alpha,
                                        int32_t* compensation)
functions.description: Computes per-column (or per-row when transposed) int32 compensation terms for unsigned 8-bit quantized GEMM using int8_t weights b, scaled by alpha. Used to adjust output biases when inputs are offset quantized.
requirements: b must point to a matrix with k*n elements if transpose_b == false (layout implied as k-by-n), or k*n elements if transpose_b == true (interpreted accordingly).

compensation must point to at least n writable int32_t elements when transpose_b == false; when transpose_b == true, the required length corresponds to the non-reduced dimension (typically k or n depending on convention); exact orientation is not documented.
k and n must be >= 0.
b and compensation must be non-null when sizes imply access.
alpha scales the compensation; exact formula is unspecified.

functions.name: ctranslate2::primitives::gemm_pack_b
functions.description: Optionally packs matrix B for GEMM. If dest is nullptr, returns the number of bytes required to store the packed data, or 0 if packing is not supported. If dest is provided, writes the packed representation of B scaled by alpha.
requirements: b must point to k*n readable elements arranged as (k-by-n) when transpose_b == false, or the transposed interpretation when true.
k and n must be >= 0.
If dest != nullptr, it must point to a buffer of at least the required packed size returned by a prior call with dest == nullptr.
b must be non-null when k*n > 0.
Returned size is in bytes (per comment). Packing support and layout are backend-dependent.

functions.name: ctranslate2::primitives::gemm
functions.description: General Matrix Multiply: computes C = alpha * op(A) * op(B) + beta * C. Supports optionally packed A or B and an optional a_shift_compensation term for quantized inputs.
requirements: Matrix dimensions must satisfy op(A) of shape (m x k) and op(B) of shape (k x n).

When a_is_packed == false: A points to a matrix with leading dimension lda; if transpose_a == false, lda >= max<dim_t>(1, k); if true, lda >= max<dim_t>(1, m). When packed, A layout is implementation-defined.

When b_is_packed == false: B points to a matrix with leading dimension ldb; if transpose_b == false, ldb >= max<dim_t>(1, n); if true, ldb >= max<dim_t>(1, k). When packed, B layout is implementation-defined.
C must point to a matrix with leading dimension ldc, with ldc >= max<dim_t>(1, n).
m, n, k must be >= 0; lda, ldb, ldc must be >= 1 for non-empty matrices.
Pointers a, b, c must be non-null when sizes imply access.
If beta == 0, C’s initial contents may be ignored; otherwise C must be initialized.
a_shift_compensation may be null when not used; if provided, it must have a layout/length expected by the backend (details unknown).

functions.name: ctranslate2::primitives::gemm_batch_strided
functions.signature:
template <ctranslate2::Device D, typename In, typename Out>
static void ctranslate2::primitives<D>::gemm_batch_strided(bool transpose_a, bool transpose_b,
                                   ctranslate2::dim_t m, ctranslate2::dim_t n, ctranslate2::dim_t k,
                                   float alpha,
                                   const In* a, ctranslate2::dim_t lda, ctranslate2::dim_t stridea,
                                   const In* b, ctranslate2::dim_t ldb, ctranslate2::dim_t strideb,
                                   float beta,
                                   Out* c, ctranslate2::dim_t ldc, ctranslate2::dim_t stridec,
                                   ctranslate2::dim_t batch_size)
functions.description: Batched GEMM with strided storage: for each batch b, computes C_b = alpha * op(A_b) * op(B_b) + beta * C_b, advancing pointers by the given strides.
requirements: batch_size must be >= 0.
A must have at least batch_size batches with pointer A + b*stridea valid for each, similarly for B and C with strideb and stridec.
Dimension and leading-dimension constraints mirror single GEMM for each batch: op(A_b) is (m x k), op(B_b) is (k x n); lda, ldb, ldc must satisfy per-batch leading dimension requirements.
Pointers a, b, c must be non-null when batch_size > 0 and sizes imply access.
If beta != 0, each C_b must be initialized before the call.

functions.name: ctranslate2::bit_cast
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename U> inline T ctranslate2::bit_cast(const U& u)
functions.description: Performs a byte-wise copy of the object representation of u into a value of type T, similar to std::bit_cast. Implemented via memcpy, it preserves the bit pattern without invoking any conversions. Intended for low-level reinterpretation of trivially copyable types of the same size.
requirements: T and U should be trivially copyable (byte-wise copy must be valid).
sizeof(T) must equal sizeof(U) to preserve the complete bit pattern and avoid overwriting/reading indeterminate bytes.
u must be a valid, non-dangling reference at the time of the call.
Endianness differences are not handled; the copy is performed as-is.

functions.name: ctranslate2::bfloat16_t::bfloat16_t
functions.description: Default constructor for the bfloat16_t wrapper type. It does not initialize the underlying bits, so the resulting value is indeterminate until explicitly assigned.
requirements: Do not read or convert the value (e.g., via operator float()) before assigning to it; the internal state is indeterminate after default construction.

functions.name: ctranslate2::bfloat16_t::operator=
functions.description: Assigns a 32-bit float to this bfloat16_t, converting the value to bfloat16 with round-to-nearest-even for normal values, mapping subnormals to signed zero, preserving infinities, and converting NaNs to quiet NaNs. Returns a reference to *this.
requirements: f can be any finite or non-finite float value (normal, zero, subnormal, infinity, NaN).
The target object must be a valid bfloat16_t instance.

functions.name: ctranslate2::bfloat16_t::operator float
functions.description: Converts this bfloat16_t back to a 32-bit float by expanding its stored 16-bit representation to a float with the upper bits filled and lower bits zeroed. Intended for reading the approximate float value represented by this bfloat16.
requirements: The bfloat16_t object should have been initialized via the float constructor or assignment before conversion; converting an indeterminate default-constructed value yields an indeterminate result.

functions.name: ctranslate2::models::ModelFactory::register_model
functions.signature:
template <typename Model, typename... Args>
bool ctranslate2::models::ModelFactory::register_model(const std::string& name, Args&&... args)
functions.description: Registers a model builder under the given name in the factory. The builder, when invoked, constructs std::make_shared<Model>(args...). Returns true if the name was newly inserted; false if a model with the same name was already present. Use to enable later creation via create_model(name).
requirements: name must be unique in the registry; if the name already exists, registration fails and returns false.
Model must be constructible from the provided Args... via std::make_shared<Model>(args...).
Model must be pointer-convertible to std::shared_ptr<ctranslate2::models::Model> (typically, Model derives from ctranslate2::models::Model).
The arguments Args... are captured by value in the stored builder; therefore each provided argument must be copyable (moves are not preserved by this implementation).
Registration must occur before calling create_model with the same name.
Exceptions thrown by Model's constructor or by copying the captured arguments will propagate during later model creation.

functions.name: ctranslate2::models::ModelFactory::create_model
functions.description: Creates and returns a new model instance previously registered under name. Looks up the builder in the registry and invokes it, returning a std::shared_ptr to the base ctranslate2::models::Model. Throws std::invalid_argument if the name is unknown.
requirements: name must correspond to a previously registered model; otherwise this function throws std::invalid_argument("Unknown model " + name).
Callers must handle exceptions both from the unknown-name case and from any exceptions thrown by the underlying Model constructor when the builder is invoked.
The returned shared_ptr is non-null on success.
Must not be called for names that have not been registered yet.

functions.name: ctranslate2::models::register_model
functions.signature:
template <typename Model, typename... Args>
bool ctranslate2::models::register_model(const std::string& name, Args&&... args)
functions.description: Convenience free function that forwards to ModelFactory::get_instance().register_model<Model>(...). Registers a model builder under name for later creation.
requirements: Same requirements as ModelFactory::register_model apply: name must be unique; Model must be constructible from Args...; Model must be pointer-convertible to std::shared_ptr<ctranslate2::models::Model>.
Because the stored builder in the factory captures arguments by value, each provided argument must be copyable (moves are not preserved by the member implementation).
Registration must occur before calling create_model with the same name.
Return value indicates success (true) or duplicate name (false).

functions.name: ctranslate2::models::create_model
functions.description: Convenience free function that creates a model instance from the global ModelFactory registry by name. Equivalent to ModelFactory::get_instance().create_model(name).
requirements: name must refer to a previously registered model; otherwise this function throws std::invalid_argument with an "Unknown model" message.

functions.name: ctranslate2::layers::MultiHeadAttention::MultiHeadAttention
functions.signature:
ctranslate2::layers::MultiHeadAttention::MultiHeadAttention(const ctranslate2::models::Model& model,

functions.description: Constructs a multi-head attention layer configured from the provided model parameters and scope. Supports self- or cross-attention, optional pre-layer normalization, decoder mode, and optional ALiBi positional bias integration.
requirements: model must outlive the construction call; it provides parameters used to initialize the layer.
scope identifies the parameter namespace inside model; must match how weights are stored.
num_heads must be > 0; determines the number of attention heads.
self_attention selects between self-attention (true) and cross-attention (false).
pre_norm selects whether layer normalization occurs before attention (true) or after (false).
is_decoder toggles decoder-specific behaviors (e.g., caching, masking).

alibi may be null; when non-null, it must describe a valid ALiBi configuration compatible with this layer and must outlive construction (if stored by pointer) or its lifetime must cover any usage required by the layer.

functions.name: ctranslate2::layers::MultiHeadAttention::operator()
functions.description: Applies multi-head attention. Computes attention between queries and values (with implicit keys derived from values or internal projections), writes the result to output, and optionally returns/uses caches, attention weights, padders, and position bias. Supports incremental decoding via cached_keys/cached_values and offset.
requirements: queries must be a valid StorageView with a shape compatible with the layer configuration (head dimension and model size). Exact expected shape layout is project-specific and not documented here; it must be consistent with values.
values must be a valid StorageView containing key/value sources. For self-attention, values typically equal the input sequence; for cross-attention, values are the encoder memory.

values_lengths, when non-null, must point to a tensor containing per-sequence lengths compatible with the batch size of queries/values; used for masking/padding. If null, no explicit length-based masking is applied.
output must be a valid StorageView and will be written in-place; its dtype and final shape should be compatible with output_type() and output_size().

cached_keys and cached_values, when non-null, must either be empty/uninitialized to receive new cache content or contain tensors whose shapes are compatible with appending at the specified offset. They enable incremental decoding; their lifetime must extend beyond the call if the cache is reused.

attention, when non-null, receives the attention weights. If return_normalized_attention is true, the weights are expected to be normalized probabilities; otherwise they may be raw scores depending on implementation.

queries_padder and values_padder, when non-null, must be configured consistently with any padding present in queries/values. They are used to map between padded and unpadded representations and must remain valid for the duration of the call.

position_bias, when non-null, supplies or receives a position bias tensor compatible with the attention score shape; if supplied, its shape must match the computed attention scores. If null, the layer may compute its own biases (e.g., relative positions, rotary, or ALiBi) depending on configuration.
offset must be >= 0; in incremental decoding it indicates the starting time index for caching/position bias.
Input tensor dtypes should be compatible with this layer; use output_type() to align output dtype.
The function is const and thread-safety depends on internal state usage; avoid concurrent calls that mutate shared cached_keys/cached_values passed by the caller.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in a fuzzer that parses
# enum name strings for ctranslate2::ComputeType via str_to_compute_type.
# We produce a seeded mixture of valid enum names (with varied casing and spacing)
# and interesting near-miss/edge strings to exercise parsing and error paths.

_VALID_TOKENS = [
    "DEFAULT",
    "AUTO",
    "FLOAT32",
    "INT8",
    "INT8_FLOAT32",
    "INT8_FLOAT16",
    "INT8_BFLOAT16",
    "INT16",
    "FLOAT16",
    "BFLOAT16",
]

# Variants to probe parser robustness: casing, whitespace, aliases, typos, unicode, extras.
_VARIANT_FUNCS = [
    lambda s, r: s,  # exact
    lambda s, r: s.lower(),
    lambda s, r: s.capitalize(),
    lambda s, r: s.replace("_", "-"),
    lambda s, r: f" {s} ",
    lambda s, r: "\t" + s + "\n",
    lambda s, r: s + ("_EXTRA" if r.random() < 0.5 else "1"),
    lambda s, r: s.replace("INT8", "int8"),
    lambda s, r: s.replace("FLOAT", "FP"),
]

_EDGE_CASES: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "\x00",  # embedded NUL
    "UNKNOWN",
    "int8",  # lowercase
    "half",  # alias-like
    "fp16",
    "float_16",
    "int8 float16",  # space instead of underscore
    "INT9",  # off-by-one
    "FLOAT33",
    "DEFAULT\x00AUTO",  # concatenated with NUL
    "AUTO\u200b",  # zero-width space
    "INT8\nFLOAT16",  # newline separated
    "  \t  ",  # whitespace
]

# Weighted pool of choices to bias towards valid tokens but include edge cases.
_DEF_WEIGHTS = {
    "valid": 0.7,
    "variant": 0.2,
    "edge": 0.1,
}

# Compose final buffer: since the target stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR once per run,
# we emit a single string as bytes (without length prefix). Fuzzer harness will
# split/consume as needed.

def _pick_variant(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rnd.choice(_VALID_TOKENS)
    fn = rnd.choice(_VARIANT_FUNCS)
    return fn(base, rnd)


def _pick_token(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    x = rnd.random()
    if x < _DEF_WEIGHTS["valid"]:
        return rnd.choice(_VALID_TOKENS)
    x -= _DEF_WEIGHTS["valid"]
    if x < _DEF_WEIGHTS["variant"]:
        return _pick_variant(rnd)
    return rnd.choice(_EDGE_CASES)


def _maybe_mix(rnd: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally surround with quotes or add leading/trailing spaces/tabs.
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        s = f'"{s}"'
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + "\r\n"
    if rnd.random() < 0.15:
        s = s.strip()  # ensure some exact forms too
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes generate multiple candidates concatenated to exercise parsers
    # that consume until first whitespace or line. But keep total under 4096 bytes.
    parts: List[str] = []
    mode = rnd.choices(["single", "line", "multiline"], weights=[0.6, 0.25, 0.15])[0]

    if mode == "single":
        token = _pick_token(rnd)
        token = _maybe_mix(rnd, token)
        parts.append(token)
    elif mode == "line":
        # Join a few tokens with spaces
        n = rnd.randint(2, 5)
        toks = [_pick_token(rnd) for _ in range(n)]
        parts.append(" ".join(toks))
    else:
        # Multiline inputs
        n = rnd.randint(2, 6)
        for _ in range(n):
            parts.append(_maybe_mix(rnd, _pick_token(rnd)))
        parts = ["\n".join(parts)]

    data = parts[0]
    # Ensure non-empty to avoid some harnesses skipping empty inputs too often.
    if not data:
        data = rnd.choice(_VALID_TOKENS)

    # Cap size to 4096 bytes.
    b = data.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")[:4096]
    return b

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for boolean-like strings without embedding literal NUL characters in the source.
# We still sometimes produce NUL bytes at runtime by constructing them dynamically.

TRUE_LITERALS = [
    "true", "True", "TRUE", "tRuE", " yes ", "y", "Y", "on", "ON", "1",
    " 1 ", "+1", "-1",
]
FALSE_LITERALS = [
    "false", "False", "FALSE", "fAlSe", " no ", "n", "N", "off", "OFF", "0",
    " 0 ", "-0", "+0",
]

EDGE_CASES = [
    "",
    " ",
    "\ttrue\n",
    # Avoid embedding NULs as literals in source; they may be inserted at runtime.
    "tru",
    "truth",
    "falsehood",
    "2", "-2",
    "NaN", "Inf", "-Inf",
    "enable", "disable",
    "yesplease", "nope",
    "T", "F",
    "On", "Off",
    " true", "false ",
]

UNICODE_CASES = [
    "ＴＲＵＥ",
    "ＦＡＬＳＥ",
    "tʀᴜᴇ",
    "fаlse",  # Cyrillic 'a'
    # NUL-like behavior will be added dynamically when needed
    "tr\nue",
    "tr ue \u200b",
]

ALL_CANDIDATES: List[str] = TRUE_LITERALS + FALSE_LITERALS + EDGE_CASES + UNICODE_CASES


def _rand_ws(rnd: random.Random):
    choices = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r", "\f"]
    left = "".join(rnd.choices(choices, k=rnd.randint(0, 3)))
    right = "".join(rnd.choices(choices, k=rnd.randint(0, 3)))
    return left, right


def _inject_runtime_nuls(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Occasionally insert NUL bytes at runtime without embedding them in source.
    if not s:
        return s.encode("utf-8")
    if rnd.random() < 0.15:
        b = bytearray(s.encode("utf-8"))
        # choose up to 2 insertion points
        count = rnd.randint(1, 2)
        for _ in range(count):
            pos = rnd.randrange(0, len(b) + 1)
            b[pos:pos] = b"\x00"
        return bytes(b)
    return s.encode("utf-8")


def _random_boolish(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rnd.random()
    if mode < 0.4:
        token = rnd.choice(TRUE_LITERALS)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        token = rnd.choice(FALSE_LITERALS)
    else:
        token = rnd.choice(ALL_CANDIDATES)

    case_mode = rnd.randint(0, 4)
    if case_mode == 1:
        token = token.upper()
    elif case_mode == 2:
        token = token.lower()
    elif case_mode == 3:
        token = token.title()

    lws, rws = _rand_ws(rnd)
    token = f"{lws}{token}{rws}"

    if rnd.random() < 0.15:
        junk_pool = ["abc", "??", "!", "xyz", "_suffix", "-trail", "\nEND"]
        token += rnd.choice(junk_pool)

    return token


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        s = _random_boolish(rnd)
    else:
        s = rnd.choice(ALL_CANDIDATES)
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            lws, rws = _rand_ws(rnd)
            s = f"{lws}{s}{rws}"

    # Limit size and encode. Optionally inject NUL bytes at runtime.
    s = s[:4000]
    data = _inject_runtime_nuls(s, rnd)
    # Append a newline, keeping total under 4096.
    if len(data) < 4095:
        data = data + b"\n"
    else:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary string
# Produce varied, valid UTF-8 text exercising split/join and prefix/suffix logic.

DELIMS = [",", " ", "\t", "\n", "::", "|", "--", ":", "..", "***"]
WHITES = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n"]
UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    "éàèçñ",
    "日本語かなカナ",
    "🙂😉🙃🤖",
    "абвгд",
    " عربى",
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCTS = "-_.,:;|/\\+*#@!$%&()[]{}<>?"


def _rand_tokens(rng: random.Random, n: int, min_len=0, max_len=12, allow_unicode=True) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    for _ in range(n):
        length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
        parts: List[str] = []
        built = 0
        while built < length:
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.6:
                k = min(length - built, max(1, rng.randint(1, length or 1)))
                chunk = "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII + PUNCTS) for _ in range(k))
            elif choice < 0.85 and allow_unicode and UNICODE_BLOCKS:
                chunk = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
            else:
                # whitespace chunk; ensure progress
                chunk = rng.choice(WHITES) or " "
            if not chunk:
                chunk = " "
            # Trim to not exceed desired length
            take = min(len(chunk), length - built)
            parts.append(chunk[:take])
            built += take
        token = "".join(parts)
        tokens.append(token)
    return tokens


def _make_joinable_segments(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    delim = rng.choice(DELIMS)
    n_segs = rng.randint(1, 8)
    segments = _rand_tokens(rng, n_segs, 1, 10)
    s = delim.join(segments)
    if rng.random() < 0.4 and delim:
        inject_idx = rng.randrange(len(s) + 1)
        s = s[:inject_idx] + delim + s[inject_idx:]
    return s


def _make_prefix_suffix_case(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 5, 20))
    pre = rng.choice(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 1, 5))
    suf = rng.choice(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 1, 5))
    variants = [
        base,
        pre + base,
        base + suf,
        pre + base + suf,
        base * rng.randint(1, 3),
        rng.choice(WHITES) + base,
        base + rng.choice(WHITES),
    ]
    return rng.choice(variants)


def _safe_choice_token(tokens: List[str], fallback_len: int = 5) -> str:
    if not tokens:
        return "x" * fallback_len
    t = random.choice(tokens)
    if not t:
        return "x" * fallback_len
    return t


def _make_token_corpus(rng: random.Random, target_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.extend(["<unk>", "<s>", "</s>"])

    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        lines.append(_make_joinable_segments(rng))

    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        lines.append(_make_prefix_suffix_case(rng))

    lines.append("")
    lines.append("  \t\t")

    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        t = rng.choice(["[", "(", "{"]) + _safe_choice_token(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 1, 6)) + rng.choice(["]", ")", "}"])
        lines.append(t)

    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        key = _safe_choice_token(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 3, 8))
        val = _safe_choice_token(_rand_tokens(rng, 1, 1, 10))
        lines.append(f"{{\"{key}\":\"{val}\"}}")

    blob = ("\n".join(lines)).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(blob) > target_bytes:
        blob = blob[:target_bytes]
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    header = rng.choice([
        "CSV,header,with,commas",
        "TSV\twith\tmixed\tseparators",
        "PIPE|sep|header",
        "DOT..sep..header",
        "STAR***sep***header",
    ])
    parts.append((header + "\n").encode("utf-8"))

    parts.append(_make_token_corpus(rng, 1500))

    ps_block = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        ps_block.append(_make_prefix_suffix_case(rng))
    parts.append(("\n".join(ps_block) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))

    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        uni = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
        s = rng.choice(PUNCTS) + uni + rng.choice(PUNCTS)
        parts.append((s + "\n").encode("utf-8"))

    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        delim = rng.choice(DELIMS)
        toks = _rand_tokens(rng, rng.randint(2, 8), 1, 8)
        parts.append((delim.join(toks) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append((rng.choice(DELIMS) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))

    parts.append(b"\n\n  \t\n")

    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
from typing import List

# Target format: text with CRLF/LF line endings, where trailing CR may be stripped.
# We generate a small but rich corpus of newline variations, including:
# - Mixed CRLF and LF
# - Lone CR (classic Mac)
# - Empty lines, long lines
# - Trailing CR before EOF, last line without newline
# - Lines with UTF-8 multibyte chars
# - Lines containing embedded NULs and other control chars (valid for std::string)
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR as an istringstream input to getline.
# We keep size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "αβγδεζηθ",        # Greek
    "こんにちは",        # Japanese
    "😀😃😄😁",         # Emoji
    "Привет",         # Cyrillic
    "العربية",         # Arabic
]

CONTROL_CHUNKS = [
    "\x00", "\x01", "\x02", "\x7f", "\t", "\f"
]

LINE_TEMPLATES = [
    "simple",
    "empty",
    "unicode",
    "control",
    "long",
]

EOLS = ["\n", "\r\n", "\r"]

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid newlines in line content; EOL added separately.
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./,:;[](){}<>?&%$#@!^*+="
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def make_line(rng: random.Random, template: str) -> str:
    if template == "simple":
        return rand_ascii(rng, 0, 24)
    if template == "empty":
        return ""
    if template == "unicode":
        chunk = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        # interleave ascii and unicode
        return rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8) + chunk + rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
    if template == "control":
        base = rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
        # sprinkle a few control bytes (not CR/LF)
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            base += rng.choice(CONTROL_CHUNKS) + rand_ascii(rng, 0, 4)
        return base
    if template == "long":
        return rand_ascii(rng, 80, 512)
    return ""

def build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct multiple lines with varied endings.
    num_lines = rng.randint(1, 25)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Ensure at least one CRLF and one LF appear to exercise both code paths.
    mandatory_lines = [
        ("abc", "\r\n"),
        ("def", "\n"),
    ]

    for content, eol in mandatory_lines:
        parts.append(content + eol)

    # Generate the remaining lines randomly.
    for _ in range(max(0, num_lines - len(mandatory_lines))):
        t = rng.choice(LINE_TEMPLATES)
        content = make_line(rng, t)
        eol = rng.choices(EOLS, weights=[4, 4, 1], k=1)[0]
        parts.append(content + eol)

    # Randomly decide whether to omit the final EOL or to end with a bare CR.
    if parts:
        # 1/3 chance to strip the last EOL entirely
        mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
        if mode == 0:
            # remove last terminator if present
            last = parts[-1]
            if last.endswith("\r\n"):
                parts[-1] = last[:-2]
            elif last.endswith("\n") or last.endswith("\r"):
                parts[-1] = last[:-1]
        elif mode == 1:
            # ensure last ends with lone CR to test CR stripping
            last = parts[-1]
            # strip any trailing newline and add CR
            if last.endswith("\r\n"):
                core = last[:-2]
            elif last.endswith("\n") or last.endswith("\r"):
                core = last[:-1]
            else:
                core = last
            parts[-1] = core + "\r"
        # else mode 2 keeps as is

    data = ''.join(parts)

    # Ensure size bound and avoid cutting in the middle of a CRLF if truncated.
    b = data.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
        # If it ends with a lone '\r', remove it to avoid accidental CRLF split; or if previous char is '\r' and we cut before '\n', drop the '\r'.
        if b.endswith(b"\r"):
            b = b[:-1]
        elif b.endswith(b"\r") or (len(b) >= 1 and b[-1] == 0x0A and len(b) >= 2 and b[-2] != 0x0D):
            pass
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_payload(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: sequences of tokens; tokens may optionally include embedded features
# separated by the Unicode separator U+FFE8. The fuzzer stub will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# to obtain token strings. We generate a compact bytes buffer containing newline-separated
# candidate tokens and small control markers. The harness typically reads chunks from the
# buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR; providing a diverse pool of tokens (ASCII, Unicode, numeric,
# punctuation, and feature-embedded variants) increases valid coverage.

SEP = "\uFFE8"  # separator used by the stub

# Build a corpus of base tokens that are safe (no whitespace) and varied.
BASE_ASCII = [
    "a", "b", "c", "the", "and", "token", "x1", "id_42", "UNK", "<s>", "</s>",
    "hello", "world", "data", "model", "_", "-", ".", ",", ":", ";", "!", "?",
]

# Include numeric-like and punctuation-only tokens to exercise edge cases.
BASE_NUM = ["0", "1", "2", "10", "123", "007", "3.14", "-1", "+5"]
PUNCT = ["..", "--", "!!!", "??", "::", ";:", "()", "[]", "{}"]

# Include some Unicode tokens (non-ASCII letters, emoji, CJK) that are single tokens.
BASE_UNICODE = [
    "é", "ñ", "über", "naïve", "北京", "東京", "Москва", "Δέλτα", "🙂", "🤖", "مرحبا",
]

# Feature fields to embed after separator.
FEATS = [
    "pos=NOUN", "pos=VERB", "lemma=be", "case=Nom", "f1", "f2", "attr=1", "attr=β",
]

# Build some precomposed feature-bearing tokens to ensure valid multi-field cases.
def make_feature_token(surface: str, feats: List[str]) -> str:
    # At least 1 feature, sometimes 2 or 3.
    k = 1 if not feats else random.randint(1, min(3, len(feats)))
    chosen = random.sample(feats, k)
    return SEP.join([surface] + chosen)

# Sometimes return a raw separator-containing token with empty features to test minimal cases.
def make_min_feature_token(surface: str) -> str:
    return surface + SEP + "f1" + SEP + "f2"

# Occasionally produce long but valid tokens (no whitespace) to test length handling.
def make_long_token() -> str:
    # Mix letters and digits, 20-80 chars.
    n = random.randint(20, 80)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:."
    return ''.join(random.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

# Produce a pool of tokens likely to be consumed by repeated FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We avoid whitespace in tokens because the consumer expects single-token strings.
def build_token_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    random.seed(rng.random())
    pool: List[str] = []

    # Start with curated bases.
    pool.extend(BASE_ASCII)
    pool.extend(BASE_NUM)
    pool.extend(PUNCT)
    pool.extend(BASE_UNICODE)

    # Add feature-bearing variations from multiple surfaces.
    surfaces = BASE_ASCII[:8] + ["surface", "feat", "tag", "node", "T", "A1", "Z"] + BASE_UNICODE[:4]
    for s in surfaces:
        pool.append(make_min_feature_token(s))
        pool.append(make_feature_token(s, FEATS))

    # Add some long tokens and numeric-like with features.
    for _ in range(10):
        lt = make_long_token()
        pool.append(lt)
        pool.append(make_feature_token(lt[:10], FEATS))

    # Ensure a few tokens that are exactly the separator-separated fields without surface variety.
    pool.append(SEP.join(["s", "f1"]))
    pool.append(SEP.join(["s", "f1", "f2", "f3"]))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order and keep size reasonable.
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for t in pool:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            uniq.append(t)
    return uniq[:512]

# The generator returns a bytes blob. Many fuzzing harnesses read consecutive calls
# from the same buffer. We structure the buffer as newline-separated tokens and add
# a small header hint containing the separator and suggested feature count values.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = build_token_pool(rng)

    # Create multiple sections to increase variety across reads:
    # - A header line that includes the separator literal and a set of integers
    #   that the harness might use for num_features or lengths.
    header_numbers = [str(n) for n in (
        rng.randint(1, 4),  # num_features (1..4)
        rng.randint(0, 8),  # sequence length hint
        rng.randint(0, 32), # batch size hint
    )]
    header = "SEP=" + SEP + "|" + ",".join(header_numbers)

    # Shuffle a view of the pool deterministically for this seed.
    tokens = pool[:]
    rng.shuffle(tokens)

    # Emit between 64 and 256 tokens to keep total size bounded.
    count = rng.randint(64, 256)
    tokens = tokens[:count]

    # Additionally craft a few tokens with dynamic features so different seeds differ.
    extras = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 15)):
        base = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)))
        extras.append(make_feature_token(base, FEATS))
    rng.shuffle(extras)

    lines: List[str] = [header] + tokens + extras
    blob = "\n".join(lines)

    # Ensure size limit <= 4096 bytes; if larger, truncate at a newline boundary.
    data = blob.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        cut = 4096
        # backtrack to previous newline to avoid cutting a token mid-byte
        nl = data.rfind(b"\n", 0, cut)
        if nl != -1:
            data = data[:nl]
        else:
            data = data[:cut]
    return data

import os
import random
import string
import struct
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path to arbitrary file data
# The fuzzer runtime will create a temp file with the provided buffer as its contents
# and pass its filename to the target. Our job is to return bytes for that file.
#
# Targets to satisfy:
# - ctranslate2::open_file_read: accepts any readable file. Content arbitrary.
# - ctranslate2::open_file_write: not constrained by initial contents, but file must exist.
# - ctranslate2::Vocabulary::from_text_file: expects a plain-text vocab, typically one token per line.
#   It may also use custom special tokens; file should be parseable as text list.
# - ctranslate2::Vocabulary::from_json_file: expects a JSON vocabulary. Provide valid JSON structure.
# - ctranslate2::models::contains_model / Model::load: likely check for a model directory structure.
#   Since FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME provides a single file, not a directory tree, keep file valid but
#   do not attempt to satisfy model loading. Our buffer still must be valid data; other stubs will bail.
#
# Strategy: Generate a valid UTF-8 text file that can be either:
#   - a plausible vocabulary text file (one token per line, include special tokens), or
#   - a valid JSON vocabulary file with common schemas used by tokenizers.
# We will randomly choose between formats to exercise both JSON and text loaders. The content remains
# <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Generate a token-like string mixing letters, digits, punctuation, and some UTF-8.
    bases = [
        string.ascii_lowercase,
        string.ascii_uppercase,
        string.digits,
        "-_#:+/",
    ]
    # Some Unicode pieces
    unicode_chunks = ["ä", "é", "ñ", "中", "文", "🙂", "Ω", "λ", "ß"]
    s = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            s.append(rng.choice(unicode_chunks))
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(bases[rng.randrange(len(bases))]))
    return "".join(s)

def _make_text_vocab(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a text vocabulary: one token per line.
    # Include a header of special tokens and a variety of tokens, ensuring uniqueness.
    num_tokens = rng.randint(50, 500)
    tokens = set()
    # Ensure common special tokens exist.
    specials = ["<unk>", "<s>", "</s>"]
    for t in specials:
        tokens.add(t)
    while len(tokens) < num_tokens:
        length = rng.randint(1, 16)
        tokens.add(_rand(rng, length))
    # Possibly add whitespace-containing tokens (quoted in many vocabs), but keep plain for simplicity.
    lines = []
    # Random chance to add leading/trailing whitespace lines to exercise trimming.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        lines.append("")
    lines.extend(tokens)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append("")
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    b = text.encode("utf-8")
    return b[:MAX_BYTES]

def _make_json_vocab(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a small but valid tokenizer vocabulary JSON structure.
    # Many loaders accept formats like:
    # {"tokens": ["<unk>", ...]} or {"vocab": {"token": id, ...}}
    # We'll choose randomly between these two common patterns.
    def json_escape(s: str) -> str:
        return (s.replace("\\", "\\\\")
                 .replace("\"", "\\\"")
                 .replace("\n", "\\n"))

    style = rng.choice(["list", "dict"])
    num_tokens = rng.randint(50, 300)
    toks: List[str] = ["<unk>", "<s>", "</s>"]
    seen = set(toks)
    while len(toks) < num_tokens:
        t = _rand(rng, rng.randint(1, 16))
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            toks.append(t)

    if style == "list":
        # {"tokens": ["...", ...], "unk_token": "<unk>", ...}
        items = ",[".join(f"\"{json_escape(t)}\"" for t in toks)
        obj = (
            "{\n"
            f"  \"tokens\": [{items}],\n"
            f"  \"unk_token\": \"{json_escape('<unk>')}\",\n"
            f"  \"bos_token\": \"{json_escape('<s>')}\",\n"
            f"  \"eos_token\": \"{json_escape('</s>')}\"\n"
            "}\n"
        )
    else:
        # {"vocab": {"token": id, ...}, "unk_token": "<unk>", ...}
        # Assign monotonically increasing ids.
        kvs = ",\n".join(
            f"    \"{json_escape(t)}\": {i}" for i, t in enumerate(toks)
        )
        obj = (
            "{\n"
            "  \"vocab\": {\n"
            f"{kvs}\n"
            "  },\n"
            f"  \"unk_token\": \"{json_escape('<unk>')}\",\n"
            f"  \"bos_token\": \"{json_escape('<s>')}\",\n"
            f"  \"eos_token\": \"{json_escape('</s>')}\"\n"
            "}\n"
        )
    b = obj.encode("utf-8")
    return b[:MAX_BYTES]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose format biased toward valid vocab parsers.
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        return _make_text_vocab(rng)
    else:
        return _make_json_vocab(rng)

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for a valid CTranslate2 text vocabulary file.
# Target stubs:
# - ctranslate2::Vocabulary::from_text_file reads from a filename provided by the fuzzer.
# - ctranslate2::models::load_vocabulary registers a file with ModelMemoryReader and expects
#   a simple text vocabulary file where each line is a token. It also expects default special
#   tokens to be resolvable (<unk>, <s>, </s>).
#
# Therefore, this generator returns a bytes buffer containing a newline-separated list of tokens.
# It always includes the specials <unk>, <s>, </s> and then adds a variety of additional tokens
# to cover different code paths: ASCII words, punctuation, Unicode, whitespace-surrounded tokens
# (trimmed by loader), repeated tokens, long tokens, and tokens containing spaces or tabs.
# The file remains valid as a vocabulary list where each line is a token.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "hello", "world", "test", "token", "example", "data", "model",
    "translate", "decoder", "encoder", "beam", "search", "greedy",
    "sample", "whisper", "audio", "text", "score", "logits", "vocab"
]

PUNCT_TOKENS = [
    ",", ".", ":", ";", "!", "?", "-", "--", "(", ")", "[", "]",
    "{", "}", "'", '"', "…", "—"
]

UNICODE_TOKENS = [
    "café", "naïve", "über", "résumé", "你好", "こんにちは", "안녕하세요",
    "😀", "¡hola!", "привет", "γειά", "مرحبا"
]

WHITESPACEY = [
    " leading", "trailing ", " both ", "with space", "tab\tinside", "multi  space"
]

DEF_CONTRACTIONS = ["don't", "it's", "we're", "they've", "o'clock"]

# Generate a token comprised of repeated characters to stress length handling.
def long_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 64, max_len: int = 512) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    ch_choices = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_"
    ch = rng.choice(ch_choices)
    # Sprinkle some variety: prefix/suffix and a few random chars
    core = ch * (length - 4)
    prefix = rng.choice(["pre_", "", "x"])  # keeps it printable
    suffix = rng.choice(["_suf", "", "y"])
    pad = max(0, length - len(prefix) - len(suffix))
    return (prefix + (ch * pad) + suffix)[:length]

# Assemble a list of diverse tokens.
def build_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens: List[str] = []

    # Required special tokens first to ensure they have stable IDs if needed.
    tokens.extend(["<unk>", "<s>", "</s>"])

    # Some common and punctuation tokens.
    rng.shuffle(ASCII_WORDS)
    tokens.extend(ASCII_WORDS[:rng.randint(5, min(12, len(ASCII_WORDS)))])

    rng.shuffle(PUNCT_TOKENS)
    tokens.extend(PUNCT_TOKENS[:rng.randint(5, min(10, len(PUNCT_TOKENS)))])

    # Unicode coverage.
    rng.shuffle(UNICODE_TOKENS)
    tokens.extend(UNICODE_TOKENS[:rng.randint(4, min(10, len(UNICODE_TOKENS)))])

    # Contractions and whitespacey entries.
    rng.shuffle(DEF_CONTRACTIONS)
    tokens.extend(DEF_CONTRACTIONS[:rng.randint(2, len(DEF_CONTRACTIONS))])

    rng.shuffle(WHITESPACEY)
    tokens.extend(WHITESPACEY[:rng.randint(2, len(WHITESPACEY))])

    # A token with spaces preserved (valid as a token line).
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        tokens.append("multi word token")
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        tokens.append("contains  two   spaces")

    # A few long tokens to trigger buffer handling paths.
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        tokens.append(long_token(rng))

    # Optionally duplicate some tokens to test deduplication/ordering paths, but keep validity.
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(tokens) > 5:
        dup = rng.choice(tokens[3:])
        tokens.append(dup)

    # Ensure tokens are unique where possible while preserving order of first occurrence,
    # but do not remove duplicates intentionally added (keep at most one duplicate event).
    seen = set()
    deduped: List[str] = []
    duplicate_kept = False
    for t in tokens:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            deduped.append(t)
        else:
            # Keep a single duplicate instance to exercise possible handling.
            if not duplicate_kept:
                deduped.append(t)
                duplicate_kept = True
    return deduped


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    tokens = build_tokens(rng)

    # Ensure size stays reasonable (<= 4096 bytes). If too large, trim extra long tokens.
    # Keep specials at the top.
    header = "\n".join(tokens[:3]) + "\n"
    body_tokens = tokens[3:]

    lines: List[str] = []
    for t in body_tokens:
        lines.append(t)
        content = header + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
        if len(content.encode("utf-8")) > 4000:
            # Remove the last added token and stop.
            lines.pop()
            break

    content = header + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    # Randomly shuffle a suffix of non-special tokens while keeping specials at head.
    if len(lines) > 3 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        suffix = lines
        rng.shuffle(suffix)
        content = header + "\n".join(suffix) + "\n"

    # Optionally append a trailing blank line or comment-like token for more variety.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        content += "\n"  # harmless extra newline
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # Add a token that looks like a comment marker; still a valid token line.
        content += "#notacommenttoken\n"

    # Final guard on size.
    data = content.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return data

import json

from typing import List, Dict, Any

# This generator produces a valid JSON vocabulary file compatible with
# ctranslate2::Vocabulary::from_json_file(std::istream&).
# CTranslate2 supports multiple vocabulary JSON layouts in practice. We'll
# generate a compact, valid schema covering common variants:
# 1) {"tokens": ["...", ...], "unk_token": "<unk>", "bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}
# 2) {"vocabulary": {"token": id, ...}, ...special tokens...}
# 3) SentencePiece-like: {"model_type": "Unigram", "vocab": [["token", score], ...], ...}
# The parser is implemented in the library and typically accepts such formats.
# We keep file size <= 4096 bytes and ensure validity.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

SPECIAL_DEFAULTS = {
    "unk_token": "<unk>",
    "bos_token": "<s>",
    "eos_token": "</s>",
}

BASIC_TOKENS = [
    "<pad>",
    "<s>",
    "</s>",
    "<unk>",
    "the",
    "a",
    "to",
    "of",
    ",",
    ".",
    "I",
    "you",
    "it",
    "##ing",
    "un",
    "##able",
    "東京",
    "😊",
]


def _rand(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def _make_token(rng: random.Random, idx: int) -> str:
    # Mix of ASCII, unicode, and subword-like pieces.
    base = [
        f"tok{idx}", f"t{idx}", f"##{idx}", f"_t{idx}",
        BASIC_TOKENS[idx % len(BASIC_TOKENS)]
    ]
    t = rng.choice(base)
    # Occasionally add diacritics/emoji/symbols
    extras = ["", "é", "ß", "ç", "中", "🙂", "-", "'", "##"]
    t += rng.choice(extras)
    return t


def _unique_tokens(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while len(tokens) < n:
        t = _make_token(rng, i)
        i += 1
        if t in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(t)
        tokens.append(t)
    return tokens


def _schema_tokens_array(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # tokens array with special tokens specified
    n = _rand(rng, 8, 256)
    toks = _unique_tokens(rng, n)
    # Ensure specials exist; if missing, prepend
    for k, v in SPECIAL_DEFAULTS.items():
        if v not in toks:
            toks.insert(0, v)
    obj = {
        "tokens": toks,
        # Randomly override specials or keep defaults
        "unk_token": rng.choice([SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["unk_token"], "<unknown>", "<unk>"]),
        "bos_token": rng.choice([SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["bos_token"], "<s>"]),
        "eos_token": rng.choice([SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["eos_token"], "</s>"]),
    }
    return obj


def _schema_vocab_map(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # map from token -> id
    n = _rand(rng, 8, 256)
    toks = _unique_tokens(rng, n)
    # Assign consecutive IDs with potential random permutation
    ids = list(range(len(toks)))
    rng.shuffle(ids)
    vocab = {t: i for t, i in zip(toks, ids)}
    obj = {
        "vocabulary": vocab,
        "unk_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["unk_token"],
        "bos_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["bos_token"],
        "eos_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["eos_token"],
    }
    return obj


def _schema_sentencepiece_like(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # SentencePiece-like minimal json
    n = _rand(rng, 8, 256)
    toks = _unique_tokens(rng, n)
    # assign random negative log probs / scores
    vocab = [[t, round(rng.uniform(-10.0, 0.0), 6)] for t in toks]
    # Ensure some specials with large scores
    specials = [SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["unk_token"], SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["bos_token"], SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["eos_token"]]
    for s in specials:
        vocab.insert(0, [s, 0.0])
    obj = {
        "model_type": rng.choice(["Unigram", "BPE", "Word", "Char"]),
        "vocab": vocab,
        "unk_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["unk_token"],
        "bos_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["bos_token"],
        "eos_token": SPECIAL_DEFAULTS["eos_token"],
    }
    return obj


def _maybe_add_metadata(rng: random.Random, obj: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    # Add optional metadata fields some loaders tolerate
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        obj["version"] = rng.choice([1, 2])
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        obj["description"] = rng.choice([
            "Toy vocabulary",
            "Auto-generated test vocabulary",
            "Multilingual vocab",
        ])


def _choose_schema(rng: random.Random) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        obj = _schema_tokens_array(rng)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        obj = _schema_vocab_map(rng)
    else:
        obj = _schema_sentencepiece_like(rng)
    _maybe_add_metadata(rng, obj)
    return obj


def _serialize_json(obj: Dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    # Compact encoding to fit within size limits
    data = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        # If too large, try to shrink by reducing tokens
        # This path trims arrays/maps when present
        def shrink_tokens_list(lst: List[Any]) -> List[Any]:
            keep = max(8, int(len(lst) * 0.5))
            return lst[:keep]
        o = obj.copy()
        if "tokens" in o and isinstance(o["tokens"], list):
            o["tokens"] = shrink_tokens_list(o["tokens"])  # type: ignore
        if "vocab" in o and isinstance(o["vocab"], list):
            o["vocab"] = shrink_tokens_list(o["vocab"])  # type: ignore
        if "vocabulary" in o and isinstance(o["vocabulary"], dict):
            items = list(o["vocabulary"].items())
            items = items[: max(8, len(items) // 2)]
            o["vocabulary"] = dict(items)
        data = json.dumps(o, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
        if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
            data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    obj = _choose_schema(rng)
    return _serialize_json(obj)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: provide an initial interesting buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as a base string
# in constructing tokens like: base_0, base_1, ... for ctranslate2::Vocabulary.
# Any arbitrary string is acceptable; we try varied, valid strings that may exercise
# different code paths (e.g., presence/absence of special tokens in the list, unicode, spaces).

MAX_LEN = 256  # keep small; overall buffer must be <= 4096 bytes


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include letters, digits, punctuation, and spaces to vary tokens
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:/@#%+="
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)).strip()


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Generate a short unicode string with a mix from selected ranges
    ranges: List[range] = [
        range(0x00A1, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplement
        range(0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        range(0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
        range(0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
        range(0x4E00, 0x4F80),   # Subset of CJK
        range(0x10A0, 0x10FF),   # Georgian
    ]
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        rr = rng.choice(ranges)
        s.append(chr(rng.choice(rr)))
    # Insert some ASCII separators to ensure clean concatenation with suffixes
    base = "".join(s)
    # Avoid empty or whitespace-only
    base = base.strip()
    return base if base else _rand_ascii(rng, min_len, max_len)


def _interesting_bases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Craft a set of interesting base strings to explore behaviors
    bases = []
    # Simple ascii alnum
    bases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 4, 16))
    # With spaces and punctuation
    bases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 8, 24))
    # Unicode-rich
    bases.append(_rand_unicode(rng, 4, 12))
    # Potential overlap with special tokens when suffixes are added
    # e.g., choosing base that ends with something like "_" to make base_unk equal to usual pattern.
    prefix = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8)
    bases.append(prefix + "_")
    # Path-like strings
    bases.append("/tmp/" + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10))
    # Email-like
    bases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8) + "@" + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 6))
    # JSONish/quoted
    bases.append('"' + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10) + '"')
    # Include model-ish tokens
    bases.append("tok")
    # Include something that could equal special tokens when combined
    # If ntokens is small, specials may not be in the token list; that’s fine.
    bases.append("special")
    # Trim to max length and ensure non-empty
    final = []
    for b in bases:
        b = b[:MAX_LEN]
        b = b if b.strip() else "base"
        final.append(b)
    return final


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = _interesting_bases(rng)
    base = rng.choice(candidates)
    # Ensure it is not excessively long and is valid UTF-8
    base = base[:MAX_LEN]
    # Return as bytes; fuzz harness will use FUZZ_PARAM_STR which interprets as string
    return base.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')

import random
from typing import List

def _make_vocab(base: str, count: int) -> List[str]:
    # Sanitize base to avoid whitespace or separators used by the parser
    base = ''.join('_' if ch in ('\t', '\n', '\r', ' ') else ch for ch in base)
    return [f"{base}_{i}" for i in range(count)]

def _make_rule(ngram: List[str], candidates: List[str]) -> str:
    # Format: "<n-gram>\t cand1 cand2 ..."
    ngram_text = ' '.join(ngram)
    cand_text = ' '.join(candidates)
    return f"{ngram_text}\t {cand_text}\n"

def _pick_distinct(rng: random.Random, pool: List[str], k: int) -> List[str]:
    k = max(1, min(k, len(pool)))
    # Ensure uniqueness for cleaner rules
    return rng.sample(pool, k)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a readable base token prefix
    base_options = [
        "tok", "w", "tkn", "sym", "x", "y", "z", "alpha", "beta", "gamma"
    ]
    base = rng.choice(base_options)

    # Vocab size: 5..24 to allow varied candidates while small enough for compact buffers
    vocab_count = rng.randint(5, 24)
    vocab = _make_vocab(base, vocab_count)

    # Number of mapping rules: 1..12
    num_rules = rng.randint(1, 12)

    # Build rules. Use mixture of unigrams and bigrams, ensure candidates exist in vocab.
    lines: List[str] = []
    for r in range(num_rules):
        use_bigram = rng.random() < 0.5 and vocab_count >= 2
        if use_bigram:
            ngram = _pick_distinct(rng, vocab, 2)
        else:
            ngram = _pick_distinct(rng, vocab, 1)
        # 2..6 candidates
        num_cand = rng.randint(2, min(6, vocab_count))
        cands = _pick_distinct(rng, vocab, num_cand)
        lines.append(_make_rule(ngram, cands))

    # Add a few deterministic, potentially overlapping rules to exercise merging and ordering
    if vocab_count >= 4:
        # unigram mapping
        lines.append(_make_rule([vocab[0]], [vocab[1], vocab[2]]))
        # bigram mapping
        lines.append(_make_rule([vocab[0], vocab[1]], [vocab[2], vocab[3]]))
    # Ensure at least one rule exists
    if not lines:
        lines.append(_make_rule([vocab[0]], [vocab[-1]]))

    # Shuffle lines for order variance
    rng.shuffle(lines)

    # Join into final text, ensure size <= 4096 bytes
    text = ''.join(lines)
    if len(text) > 4096:
        # Trim safely at line boundaries
        acc = []
        total = 0
        for line in lines:
            if total + len(line) > 4096:
                break
            acc.append(line)
            total += len(line)
        text = ''.join(acc)

    return text.encode('utf-8')
